titulo: Why does your phone die at 40% in the cold? (Apple: designed for 32 to 95 F; battery recovers when warmed)
receta: error cotidiano con regla para guardar (rango de temperatura) + pregunta de una palabra
destinatario: Se lo manda alguien cuyo celular se apagó en la fila del recital a su amigo que dice que la batería está rota.

interaccion.guardar: iPhones are designed for 32 to 95 F. Too cold: battery life can get shorter and it can shut off. Warm it up and battery life returns to normal.
interaccion.comentar: What percent was your phone at when it last died in the cold?

fuentes: Apple Support, If your iPhone or iPad gets too hot or too cold

frases.texto: Your phone says forty percent, then it just dies in the cold.

frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Apple says iPhones are designed for temperatures between thirty-two and ninety-five degrees Fahrenheit.
In very cold conditions, the battery life can get temporarily shorter, and the phone could shut itself off.
The good news: Apple says battery life returns to normal when the phone gets back to higher temperatures.
Heads up: Apple also says not to leave your phone in a parked car, where the temperature can go outside that range.
Save this for the next cold day.
